column2: The selected chapter begins at 2; no regnal formula is invented at 1. Saul's three thousand divide into two thousand with him and one thousand with Jonathan, with locations and dismissal of the rest to individual tents retained.

Jonathan strikes Nasib the foreigner, the foreigners hear, and Saul trumpets the slaves' rebellion throughout the land. Nasib and the declaration are not replaced by garrison and let the Hebrews hear.
The circulating report attributes the blow to Saul although verse 3 names Jonathan; both reports remain. Israel's shame and the people's cry after Saul at Gilgal are preserved without harmonization.
Thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen and sand-like multitude accompany repeated ascent and encampment at Michmash opposite Baithon toward the south.
column3: The selected number and direction remain despite familiar alternatives; no numerical correction is inferred from historical plausibility alone.

column2: Israel's collective distress and inability to advance precede hiding in five kinds of shelter: caves, enclosures, rocks, trenches and pits.
column3: Could not advance interprets the compressed negative infinitive me prosagein auton; exact subject and construal remain open, not treated as fully resolved syntax.

column2: Crossing people cross the Jordan into Gad and Gilead, while Saul remains at Gilgal and the people behind him are terrified. The repeated crossing is retained rather than converted to an ethnic label.
Seven-day waiting for the testimony as Samuel said precedes Samuel's non-arrival and the people's scattering away from Saul.
column3: Testimony for martyrion is provisional in this timing context; the record does not silently replace the selected noun with an appointed deadline.

column2: Saul orders bringing forward for whole burnt and peace offerings, then offers the whole burnt offering. Them supplies the unstated object of bring from the sacrificial context; completion of both offering types is not asserted.
Samuel's arrival coincides with completion of the whole burnt offering; Saul goes out to meet and bless him. The stated blessing purpose is not reduced to a neutral greeting.

Propose Because at Saul's explanation and a continuing comma into verse 12. The scattering people, Samuel's failure to arrive as ordered at the testimony of days, and the foreigners' gathering remain grounds for Saul's following statement.
column3: Because supplies the overt hoti relationship; the awkward testimony-of-days phrase remains unresolved rather than replaced from another source.

column2: Saul's quoted expectation of attack and failure to entreat the Lord's face precede mastering himself and offering. The bodily face image and his stated self-restraint are retained.
column3: Mastered myself for enekrateusamen is provisional; forced myself is an alternative, but neither implies narrator endorsement of Saul's justification.

column2: It has come to nothing for you, my commandment commanded by the Lord, and the Lord's preparation of the kingdom for ever remain.
column3: The relation of hos nyn and the prepared kingdom is difficult; inherited had prepared is provisional and does not silently introduce a complete counterfactual would-have-established clause.

column2: The kingdom's failure to stand contrasts with the Lord's future seeking a man according to His heart and appointing him ruler because Saul failed to keep all commanded things.
column3: The future verbs remain future, without naming David before the narrative does.

column2: Samuel's departure on his way, the remnant following Saul to meet after the fighting people, the journey to Benjamin's Gibeah and about six hundred mustered men all remain.
column3: The compressed meeting/following sequence has uncertain attachment and implied objects; no separate army is invented to clarify it.

column2: Saul, Jonathan and their people stay in Geba and weep, while foreigners are encamped at Michmash. The selected weeping clause is retained.
A destroying force comes from the foreigners' country in three companies; the first faces Gophera toward Sogal. Force supplies the collective sense of the destroying participle.
The other two companies face Beth-horon and Geba overlooking Gai the Sabin. The selected geographical sequence is retained without substituting a familiar wilderness description.
Absence of an ironworker throughout Israel is explained by the foreigners' intent to prevent Hebrew sword and spear production. The source's two weapon terms remain.
All Israel goes down for forge work on reaping tool, implement, axe and sickle; each man's possession is retained without identifying an uncertain generic implement more narrowly.
The ready vintage, three shekels per tooth for implements and the same rate for axe and sickle remain; no alternative fractional price is substituted.
column3: Tool identities, the harvest wording and hypostasis as rate remain lexical questions, and no modern currency conversion is made.

column2: During the Michmash war the people's lack of sword and spear contrasts with their presence with Saul and Jonathan. The two leaders are the stated exceptions without an added arsenal description.
A singular implicit subject goes out from the foreigners' station beyond Michmash; inherited he retains that unusual construction.
column3: The abrupt subject and accusative phrase leave the syntax unresolved; the text is not silently regularized into a garrison going out to the pass.
